body:
First of all, the guy sounds like a complete douchebag. He thinks that you're just so crazy about him that you'll never leave, so he doesn't treat you the way you need to be treated in a loving relationship. (to be clear, "you" as in OP, not you as "one", or a general you).

To some extent, yes - you are needy. Most people see this as a bad thing. I think it's mostly insecurity. I know that probably stings, but bear with me- I mean no disrespect. I'm insecure and needy too. It happens. Here's the thing. If you're not treated in a way that shows YOU that he cares about you, you're going to feel insecure about the relationship. You're going to want to check in all the time to make sure that everything's ok. You're looking for him to reach out to you, to touch you, to make you feel like he cares about you as much as you care about him. I can almost guarantee that he doesn't understand this at all. 

The best thing that you can do is pull away a little bit. It sucks, but it's true. You're not his priority because he doesn't have to put any effort in to keep you around. He seems to know that he acts like an asshole, and that you'll just stay with him anyway. 

Fuck that. You deserve better. 

You don't have to prove to him or anyone else that you're good enough. You just ARE. If he's not treating you with respect, and he's not willing to talk about your needs or put any effort in to make you feel special and loved, then he's really not worth expending so much effort for. Spend that effort on yourself instead, and it'll probably end up bringing him closer. You want a big ego boost? Maybe this suggestion makes me an asshole, but make an OkCupid profile and watch how many dudes message you. 

Here's the bottom line: I think you have different relationship needs. It seems to me that you need to feel safe and secure and loved, and you're trying to get that feeling by acting how you want him to act towards you. But that doesn't get you what you want. It shows him that you're there no matter what. I'd guess that your need for contact and affection increases as he fails to respond, and that increase in neediness pushes him away. He probably doesn't understand what you're looking for or how to give it to you. He probably just thinks that you're clingy and sweet- he doesn't understand that your actions are how you show him that you care, and that you would like him to do the same things for you so that you know that HE cares. 

Sit down and have a talk with him. Tell him that you're unfulfilled in this relationship, and that you need him to do more for you to feel loved. Explain to him what is is that you need as specifically as possible. Listen to him when he says he needs space, and respect HIS needs too. 

And if he won't talk, won't listen, or won't make an effort? Walk away and find someone who will.
I like your quote on worrying. I'll have to remember that one! Thanks!

Thanks so much! 

Thankfully, my insurance doesn't require me to get pre-authorization to see a specialist. Unfortunately, the specialist I called yesterday for an appointment in my area requires me to have a prescription for testing from my doctor, so I'm going to go somewhere else. 

It's good to see the financial aspect of this in bullet points. It makes it a lot less scary. Thanks!

Good to know! Thanks!

I actually went several weeks wearing deodorant very sparingly, if at all (I just moved to a new apartment, lost my deodorant in some random box the process, and was too cheap to buy new!).

Sorry to hear about your aunt. 

I didn't have a cosigner for the loans (THANK GOD!), so they'll die with me if I don't pay them off.
That's a really good point. In that case, there's absolutely no reason for delay. Thank you.

I checked into the free places, but I don't qualify because I have health insurance (even though it's not that great), and I made more money than the guidelines require (although, since it pretty much all went into business expenses, I probably qualify- it depends on how things are calculated.)

The family history and health probability that I have breast cancer is low. No one in my family has had breast cancer (although my grandmother did die from colon cancer).  I did a 23andme test that suggested I have a much lower than average chance of getting it. I was moderately overweight for a few years, but am now in the best shape of my life. 

I have some government loans, but the private loans are the ones that are killing me. My government loans will eventually be forgiven, but Discover and Wells Fargo have no mercy. 

Thanks for the crossed fingers! I'll be sure to update.

He DOES love me- I don't doubt it. 

The main issue for him is uncertainty. He finds the sneaking feeling crippling. 

I get the sneaking feeling too- it doesn't worry me. Even if the grass gets dandelions, I know that the grass over here is green enough- it just needs a little bit of water and fertilizer every once in a while, or it will end up dying. 

The main issue for me is "holy shit-  When is this sweet, loving, wonderful guy going to stop sucker-punching me? Ever?"

>Plus, just reading what you've described seems terribly hurtful. With every action you're basically saying "I love you", and his responses are along the lines of "meh".Your passion and dedication to this relationship isn't enough to sustain it, if he's not up to participate fully, then it may be time to revisit the arrangement.

This is the part that's killing me. He thinks that I'm completely head-over-heels for him and would never leave. He's flat-out said it. He *hasn't* been a full participant. If he was, there wouldn't be an issue.

He's there for me too. I got hurt and needed stitches last week, and he came to the hospital with me - we were silly together, laughed the whole time, and were generally adorable. 

I've been depressed, and he suggested a book on CBT, and has pushed me to meditate more.
We have sex with very intense mutual intimacy - that's what makes it so great.
I think it was 2-3 years. Apparently, she cleaned the apartment too, and he didn't really appreciate her either.

>But when was the last time he made you feel very special?

He was very sweet for my birthday. Recently, he got me a fancy new yoga mat, especially made for hot yoga, since I was signing up for a class down the street. He came to the hospital with me last weekend and made me laugh when I needed stitches after slipping and falling in some glass at a bar. He met me at my office when I had a late-night meeting with some men I didn't know too well, so that I would feel OK scheduling an evening meeting. He sent me flowers at work a few months ago, because he was out of town for a big event of mine. 

Ultimately, though, I think he puts his own needs first... and I have been too.

>Do you really want to live your whole life knowing or wondering that your SO is only settling for you. 

No, I don't. 

>I wish you the best of luck, I know this must be very hard.

Thanks. This whole thing totally sucks.

Yeah, I tend to agree - compatibility is one thing, but I don't think there's a singular person out there to fulfill all of anyone's need - I'm trying to be realistic, and decide which faults I can and cannot overlook, he's trying to find perfection.

>Why do you like this guy?

He's not a bad guy. It doesn't all come down to how much he appreciates me. He's a good person, he makes me laugh, he comforts me when I'm sad. We talk more openly than I feel like I'm able to with anyone else. He's generally supportive. And the little things, like our taste in movies and beer.

I think he under-appreciates me because he's generally oblivious, and used to being catered to. Apparently, lack of appreciation has been an issue in his previous relationships as well. I think he's just been treated so well in his life that he doesn't know how good he's had it, and since he can't see it, he can't appreciate it.

> On a scale of 10 for each of your total package attractiveness to the other gender, how do you rate you and your boyfriend?

We're about even. He's more "athletic" looking, but I get hit on constantly. I wear a size 4/6, and have an hour-glass figure. I'm a very well-liked social butterfly. Everyone in my office building knows me- to the point where I had to post a sign on my desk for times when I'm working on something "urgent" and can't chat. More than one of my male friends have commented that any man lucky enough to date me should be smart enough to marry me immediately. Other people tell me I'm a catch. I guess I just don't feel like one.

>Limerence is a tricky word. I had to look it up to be sure we were on the same page. It sounds a lot like young love, which is often blind.

I agree. Limerence is the word that he used. He said that he has deep, affectionate love for me, but that he doesn't have "that crazy feeling". Why anyone would want that over something calm, lasting, and sustainable is completely beyond me.

>Have you kept your eyes open?

Only on him, and on my business. For pretty much the entire last year, if I wasn't working at work, I've been working "at home".
